summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Teleport to a far away structure such as a woodland mansion or pillager outpost that may contain naturally generated allays.
2. Observe whether the chunks near you are loading in.
3a. If the chunks are not loading in, reload chunks using `F3 + A`.
4. Observe whether the chunks load in after reloading.
5a. If the chunks still do not load in, you have successfully reproduced this bug.
5b. If the chunks do load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the structure; try teleporting closer.
6. If the server hangs while the chunks are not loading, attempt to save your world.
7. Observe that you are unable to save your world and must force crash the game.
Observed Behavior: The actual behavior of the game when encountering the issue involves the server hanging and the game becoming unresponsive upon loading chunks that contain structures with naturally generated allays. After teleporting several thousand blocks away, players experience a complete halt in chunk loading, even though the F3 menu and other UI elements can still be accessed; however, they do not function as expected. The F3 menu remains stuck, consistently displaying an internal server tick rate of 18ms, which indicates that while the server is still running, it is unable to process any chunk loading. Attempts to reload chunks using the F3 + A command do not resolve the issue, and during this server hang, commands become unresponsive. Occasionally, a small number of chunks, ranging from two to eight, may load if the player is not located within the structure containing the allays. If a player tries to save their world during this state, the game will prevent the save, forcing the player to crash the game to exit, which results in the loss of any unsaved data. It is important to note that summoning an allay using the "/summon allay" command does not trigger this problem, nor does visiting a woodland mansion without naturally generated allays. The issue is specifically linked to structures that contain allays that spawn naturally in the game. To reproduce this bug, players must teleport to a distant structure like a woodland mansion or pillager outpost, observe the loading state of nearby chunks, and if they do not load, attempt to reload them. If the chunks still do not load after these attempts, the bug is successfully reproduced. Players should ensure they are using the correct version of Minecraft, specifically version 22w13a, as the bug may not occur in future snapshots. In the event of a hang, players are advised against using the F3 + C command or ALT + F4 to exit, as these methods are ineffective; instead, they should use task management tools specific to their operating system to terminate the game process.
Expected Behavior: When teleporting to a structure containing naturally generated allays, the game should seamlessly load all nearby chunks, allowing players to explore without interruption. The F3 menu should display real-time server tick information and respond to commands effectively. Players should be able to save their world without issues, and allays should function normally, gathering and delivering items as intended. The experience should remain stable, with no server hangs or crashes occurring during gameplay.
